explain.es: En inglés, el pasado tiene un segundo trabajo: expresar distancia de la realidad. Tras estructuras como would rather, it's time, as if o suppose, un verbo en pasado (went, knew, didn't) habla del presente o del futuro, pero de forma irreal, deseada o hipotética. Es el equivalente de muchos subjuntivos del español: prefiero que te quedes → I'd rather you stayed. Para referirnos a algo irreal en el pasado, damos un paso más atrás: past perfect (had gone). (Wish e if only, de la misma familia, se trabajan en B2.)
explain.en: The past tense can express distance from reality. After would rather, it's time, as if or suppose, a past form refers to the present or future in an unreal way. For the unreal past, we step back again: past perfect.
formula: would rather / it's time / as if + *pasado simple* + = irreal ahora
would rather / as if / suppose + *past perfect* + = irreal antes

explain.title: 1 · Would rather / would sooner
explain.es: would rather (contracción 'd rather) y su variante menos frecuente would sooner significan preferiría. Si el sujeto es el mismo, van con infinitivo sin to: I'd rather stay in. Si hablamos de lo que preferimos que haga otra persona, usamos sujeto + pasado, aunque hablemos del presente o del futuro: I'd rather you stayed in (prefiero que te quedes). Negativas: I'd rather not + infinitivo / I'd rather you didn't + infinitivo, una forma muy educada de pedir que alguien no haga algo.
explain.en: would rather / would sooner + bare infinitive (same subject); + another subject + past simple (present or future meaning). Negatives: I'd rather not…, I'd rather you didn't…

examples.en: I'd rather work from home tomorrow, if that's all right.
examples.es: Preferiría trabajar desde casa mañana, si no hay problema.

examples.en: I'd rather you didn't mention this to anyone.
examples.es: Preferiría que no se lo comentaras a nadie.

examples.en: My parents would sooner I studied law than drama.
examples.es: Mis padres preferirían que estudiara Derecho en vez de Arte Dramático.

explain.title: Truco del paso atrás
explain.es: Piensa en el pasado como una distancia: alejarse en el tiempo = alejarse de la realidad. Un paso atrás (presente → pasado) = irreal ahora. Dos pasos atrás (presente → past perfect) = irreal en el pasado. Y donde en español pondrías subjuntivo (prefiero que vengas, ya es hora de que te vayas, como si fuera), en estas estructuras el inglés pone pasado.
explain.en: Past = distance from reality. One step back = unreal now; two steps back = unreal past. Where Spanish uses the subjunctive, English uses the past.

explain.title: Todas las formas de WOULD RATHER
head: Estructura
Tiempo
Ejemplo
Traducción
rows: I'd rather walk than wait for the bus.
Prefiero andar que esperar el autobús.
explain.note: would sooner sigue exactamente los mismos patrones. Respuesta corta muy útil: Shall I tell him? — I'd rather you didn't.
explain.note_en: would sooner follows the same patterns. Useful reply: I'd rather you didn't.

explain.title: WOULD RATHER, WOULD PREFER o PREFER
explain.title_en: would rather, would prefer or prefer?
explain.es: Las tres expresan preferencia, pero cada una tiene su propia gramática. ¡Ojo con el to y con than / to!
explain.en: All three express preference, but each has its own grammar.

cols.head: 🙏 would rather
items: A than B: I'd rather go than stay.

cols.head: 🤝 would prefer
items: + it if + pasado: I'd prefer it if you went.
+ objeto + to: I'd prefer you to go.

cols.head: 💚 prefer (en general)
items: A to B: I prefer tea to coffee.

explain.title: 2 · Preferencias sobre el pasado
explain.es: Para expresar una preferencia sobre algo que ya ocurrió, damos un paso atrás: would rather + otro sujeto + past perfect (I'd rather you had told me = habría preferido que me lo dijeras). Si el sujeto es el mismo, usamos would rather have + participio: I'd rather have stayed at home (habría preferido quedarme en casa). En ambos casos, lo que pasó en realidad fue lo contrario.
explain.en: Preferences about the past: would rather + subject + past perfect, or would rather have + past participle (same subject). What actually happened was the opposite.

examples.en: I'd rather you had asked me before inviting them.
examples.es: Habría preferido que me preguntaras antes de invitarlos.

examples.en: She'd rather they hadn't published the photos.
examples.es: Ella habría preferido que no publicaran las fotos.

examples.en: To be honest, I'd rather have gone to the beach.
examples.es: Sinceramente, habría preferido ir a la playa.

explain.title: 3 · It's time / high time / about time
explain.es: It's time + sujeto + pasado significa ya es hora de que…: algo debería estar pasando ya y no pasa. Con high o about añadimos impaciencia, crítica o ironía (ya va siendo hora). Si no hay crítica y solo constatamos que ha llegado el momento, usamos it's time (for + persona) + to + infinitivo. Ojo: tras it's (high) time + sujeto no se usa ni el presente ni el past perfect.
explain.en: It's (high / about) time + subject + past simple: something should already be happening (often critical). Neutral: It's time (for sb) to + infinitive.

examples.en: It's high time the government tackled the housing crisis.
examples.es: Ya va siendo hora de que el Gobierno aborde la crisis de la vivienda.

examples.en: It's about time you found a proper job!
examples.es: ¡Ya es hora de que te busques un trabajo como Dios manda!

examples.en: It's time we were going — it's nearly midnight.
examples.es: Ya es hora de que nos vayamos: es casi medianoche.

examples.en: It's time for the children to go to bed.
examples.es: Es hora de que los niños se vayan a la cama.

explain.title: 4 · As if / as though
explain.es: as if y as though (como si) son intercambiables. Tras ellos, el pasado indica que la comparación es irreal o improbable: He talks as if he knew everything (no lo sabe todo). Si la comparación es probable o real, usamos el tiempo normal: It looks as if it's going to rain. Para algo irreal anterior: past perfect (as if he had seen a ghost). En registro formal se prefiere were con todas las personas; en lenguaje coloquial muchos nativos usan like. Expresiones: It's not as if + pasado = ¡ni que…!; As if! = ¡ni de broma!
explain.en: as if / as though + past = unreal comparison; + present = likely. Past perfect for an earlier unreal situation. Formal: were. It's not as if… = ¡ni que…!

examples.en: He behaves as if he owned the company.
examples.es: Se comporta como si fuera el dueño de la empresa.

examples.en: She looked as though she had seen a ghost.
examples.es: Tenía cara de haber visto un fantasma.

examples.en: Don't talk to me as if I were a child.
examples.es: No me hables como si fuera un niño.

examples.en: It sounds as if the meeting is going well.
examples.es: Parece que la reunión va bien.

explain.title: 5 · Suppose / imagine / what if
explain.es: Suppose, Supposing, Imagine y What if (imagina que…, ¿y si…?) introducen hipótesis. Con pasado, la situación es improbable o imaginaria (presente o futuro); con past perfect, imaginamos un pasado distinto; con presente, la posibilidad es real. La oración principal suele llevar would (o would have para el pasado). (Supposing como alternativa a if se amplía en las condicionales avanzadas.)
explain.en: Suppose / Supposing / Imagine / What if + past = unlikely or imaginary; + past perfect = imagined past; + present = real possibility.

examples.en: Suppose you were offered a job in Tokyo — would you take it?
examples.es: Imagina que te ofrecieran un trabajo en Tokio: ¿lo aceptarías?

examples.en: Imagine we didn't have the internet. How would we work?
examples.es: Imagina que no tuviéramos internet. ¿Cómo trabajaríamos?

examples.en: Suppose it rains tomorrow — have we got a plan B?
examples.es: Pongamos que mañana llueve: ¿tenemos un plan B?

explain.title: AS IF + presente o + pasado
explain.es: El tiempo verbal revela lo que piensa el hablante: ¿es posible o cierto, o es imaginario?
explain.en: The tense shows whether the speaker thinks it is likely or imaginary.

cols.head: ✅ Probable → presente
items: You look as if you need a rest. (Probablemente sí.)

cols.head: 🎭 Irreal → pasado
items: He spends as if he were a millionaire. (No lo es.)
She treats me as though I didn't exist.

explain.title: Resumen del unreal past
head: Estructura
Irreal ahora / futuro
Irreal en el pasado
Alternativa «real» o neutra
rows: I'd have preferred it if you had stayed.
explain.note: Regla de oro: pasado = irreal en el presente; past perfect = irreal en el pasado. Con el verbo be, el registro formal prefiere were: as if I were…, suppose he were…; was es coloquial.
explain.note_en: Golden rule: past = unreal now; past perfect = unreal past. Formal English prefers were.

items.es: Identifica la estructura: would rather, it's time, as if, suppose…
Con would rather, ¿es el mismo sujeto? → infinitivo sin to. ¿Otro sujeto? → sujeto + pasado.
items.en: Same subject → bare infinitive; another subject → past.

items.es: ¿Es irreal en el presente o futuro? → pasado simple (were, didn't, went).
items.en: Unreal now or in the future → past simple.

items.es: ¿Es irreal en el pasado? → past perfect (had gone), excepto con it's time.
items.en: Unreal past → past perfect (not after it's time).

items.es: ¿Es probable o real (as if, suppose)? → tiempo normal (presente).

“It's high time we left.” → We should already be leaving.

exercises.text_title: Ask Amanda: “My colleague acts as if he were my boss”
text: Dear Amanda, I've worked in the same team as Greg for three years. Although we have the same job title, he behaves as if he were in charge of the whole department. He hands out tasks, comments on my emails and talks to me as though I had joined the company yesterday. I'd rather he didn't involve himself in my work, but I don't want to cause a scene. Suppose I complained to our manager — would that make things worse? — Fed up in Bristol

Dear Fed up, it's high time you stood up for yourself. Greg probably doesn't realise how he comes across, so I'd rather you spoke to him before going to your manager. Imagine you were in his position: wouldn't you prefer a quiet word to a formal complaint? Choose a calm moment and say something like: “I'd prefer it if you let me manage my own emails.” If nothing changes, then it will be time to involve your manager. And remember: it's not as if you were asking for anything unreasonable.

items.q: Greg is the writer's boss.
items.why: They have the same job title; he only behaves as if he were the boss.

items.q: The writer wants to cause a scene.
items.why: “I don't want to cause a scene.”

items.q: How does Greg talk to the writer?
items.a: As though the writer had joined the company yesterday.

items.q: What would the writer rather Greg didn't do?
items.a: Involve himself in the writer's work.

items.q: Amanda advises going straight to the manager.
items.why: She'd rather the writer spoke to Greg first.

items.q: What sentence does Amanda suggest saying to Greg?
items.a: “I'd prefer it if you let me manage my own emails.”

items.q: Find an example of it's high time + past in the reply.
items.a: “It's high time you stood up for yourself.”

items.q: What does Amanda mean by “it's not as if you were asking for anything unreasonable”?
items.a: That the writer's request is perfectly reasonable.

items.a: Ej.: Suppose I won a scholarship to study abroad — I would go to Canada.

checklist.es: Uso would rather / would sooner + infinitivo o + sujeto + pasado.
checklist.en: I can use would rather / would sooner correctly.

checklist.es: Expreso preferencias sobre el pasado con past perfect o would rather have.
checklist.en: I can express preferences about the past.
I can distinguish would rather, would prefer and prefer.

checklist.es: Uso it's (high / about) time + pasado y it's time to…
checklist.en: I can use it's (high) time + past and it's time to…

checklist.es: Elijo presente o pasado tras as if / as though según sea real o irreal.
checklist.en: I can choose the right tense after as if / as though.

checklist.es: Planteo hipótesis con suppose, imagine, what if.
checklist.en: I can imagine situations with suppose, imagine, what if.
